text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Police picked up over 300 activists of different political parties in night-long raids after the killing of power utility KESC chief Shahid Hamid and two others on Saturday.
- The Chief Justice of Supreme Court, Justice Sajjad Ali Shah, has said that he would initiate suo motu proceedings to look into the deteriorating law and order situation in Karachi.
- Pakistan resumes its diplomatic drive to bring warring Afghan factions to the negotiating table with the departure of Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan to Moscow.
- Ten people, including two minibus drivers, were killed and another 28 injured when two minibuses collided near Chisht Nagar, 16 km south of Multan.

- A Pakistan delegation led by Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz which came to New York to solicit money from the Association of Pakistani Physicians of North America convinced them to contribute towards the prime minister's debt retirement fund.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- Nationalised commercial banks and development finance institutions have failed to evolve a homogeneous policy to implement the package announced by the Governor of State (central) Bank of Pakistan for the recovery of stuck-up loans from the industrial sector.
- Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar said the government is working on a plan to check smuggling which is adversely affecting legal trade and government revenues.
- Pakistan has invited foreign companies to establish industrial zones alongside the Lahore-Islamabad motorway.
THE NATION
- A five-member IMF mission arrives on Wednesday to negotiate a $1.5 billion enhanced structural adjustment facility for Pakistan.
THE MUSLIM
- As many as 26 people died of sun-stroke as the mercury soared to 43.5 degrees celsius in some parts of the country.
Z Motorcycle-riding gunmen shot dead a militant Sunni Moslem leader in the city of Faisalabad in Punjab province.
THE NEWS
- A seven-member commission is being set up to lay off surplus staff at government departments and public sector corporations.
- The government is amending the 60-year-old insurance act to reform the functions of this sector.
- The government plans to reorganise the Federal Investigating Agency and limit the scope of its investigation.
